question: What filesystem boundary should OpenClaw expose for this request: a canonical `tools.fs` allow/deny path policy, a narrower workspace-only extension, or OS/container isolation only?
rationale: The requested behavior defines a public config surface and security boundary, and the live issue already has product/security review labels plus competing implementation designs.

options.title: Settle one `tools.fs` path-policy contract
options.body: Choose a canonical config shape with deny precedence, normalization/symlink behavior, explicit exec scope, docs, and security tests before landing an implementation.

options.title: Split exec from file-tool policy
options.body: Land a file-tool-only policy only if shell-mediated file access is explicitly tracked and documented as outside the first version.

options.title: Defer to OS/container isolation
options.body: Decline host path ACL config if maintainers decide OpenClaw should rely on user permissions and sandbox backends beyond workspaceOnly.

recommendation.title: Settle one `tools.fs` path-policy contract
recommendation.body: Choose a canonical config shape with deny precedence, normalization/symlink behavior, explicit exec scope, docs, and security tests before landing an implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest combination of prior review context and workspaceOnly/security-boundary history for deciding this public config direction.
